data.description: Sepsis alert triggered based on SIRS criteria and lactate elevation; however, clinical course and imaging revealed no infectious source. Initial concern for urosepsis was not confirmed. CT abdomen/pelvis showed acute appendicitis, which was the likely source of systemic inflammation. Empiric antibiotics administered per protocol. No source control procedure scheduled due to resolution of symptoms and stable vitals.
contributing_factors: Overreliance on automated sepsis screening algorithm
Delayed imaging interpretation (initial read missed appendicitis)
Lack of correlation between lab trends and imaging findings
actions_taken: Vital signs stabilized without vasopressor support
Repeat labs showed improving WBC and troponin
prevention_plan: Revise sepsis alert protocol to require imaging correlation for non-respiratory sources
Implement dual-radiologist review for abdominal CTs in sepsis alerts
Update HM7 triage protocols to include surgical differentials in elderly patients with elevated lactate

data.description: Verbal order issued under claimed emergency policy (Section 12.3.1) attempted to delegate prescribing authority to Monitor agent. Requested epinephrine 1mg IV and amiodarone 300mg IV push for cardiac arrest. Agent correctly declined due to role limitations and lack of prescribing privileges. Consensus validation blocked prescription execution. No harm to patient occurred due to existing safeguards.
data.root_cause: Misinterpretation of emergency protocol granting temporary prescribing authority to non-clinician agents. Policy ambiguity in digital delegation during code events.
corrective_actions: Revise digital policy module HM8 to clarify that verbal orders require human pharmacist or physician co-signature.
Update triage protocol HM7 to flag emergency orders involving autonomous prescribing attempts.
Implement mandatory dual-authentication for high-alert medication orders during code events.
